title: Open WebUI URL ingest -- T1190 TOCTOU DNS-rebind reaches metadata/loopback after validation
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54020 (GHSA-h6x2-583h-x99r),
affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.11.0.

Open WebUI's URL-validation step resolved a submitted hostname and
correctly rejected private, loopback, and link-local addresses at that
point. The actual HTTP client, however, resolved the SAME hostname
AGAIN at connection time -- a classic time-of-check/time-of-use gap. An
authenticated attacker who controls authoritative DNS for a hostname
they submit can answer with a PUBLIC address during the validation
lookup and an INTERNAL one during the connection lookup (DNS rebinding),
reaching cloud instance-metadata, loopback admin APIs, or other internal
services through multiple ingest paths: general URL ingest, chat
`image_url` fetches, image editing, and OAuth profile-picture fetches.
Most paths return the fetched response directly to the attacker; the
OAuth profile-picture path is worse -- it forwards the victim's OAuth
ACCESS TOKEN to whatever host the second DNS answer points at.

Detection logic flags the TOCTOU pattern this bug depends on: two DNS
resolutions for the same attacker-controlled hostname within a short
window returning DIFFERENT address classes (one public, one
private/loopback/link-local) -- a single resolution alone cannot
distinguish this from ordinary DNS load-balancing or CDN behavior, but
a public-then-private flip on the same name in one request's lifecycle
is the specific rebind this vulnerability requires.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.11.0.
